title: Ammonia Derivatives & Brady’s Reagent (2,4-DNP Diagnostic Test)
topics: 3. Carbonyl Reaction with Primary Amine Derivatives (H₂N-Z) at Controlled pH 3.5
Ammonia Derivatives Matrix: Hydroxylamine (Oxime), Hydrazine (Hydrazone), Phenylhydrazine, 2,4-DNP, Semicarbazide
Brady’s Reagent (2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine in Methanol/Acid): Universal Yellow/Orange/Red Crystalline Diagnostic
CRITICAL NEST TRAP: Semicarbazide Nucleophilicity Selection (H₂N⁽¹⁾-NH-CO-NH₂⁽²⁾)
Resonance Delocalization of the Amide -NH₂ rendering it Non-Nucleophilic
quickSummary: Carbonyls condense with H₂N-Z at pH ~3.5 to form >C=N-Z imine derivatives. Brady's Reagent (2,4-DNP) forms yellow/orange/red crystalline precipitates with all aldehydes and ketones. In semicarbazide (H₂N⁽¹⁾-NH-CO-NH₂⁽²⁾), only NH₂⁽¹⁾ acts as a nucleophile because NH₂⁽²⁾ is resonance-delocalized into C=O.
summary: Master the ammonia derivative condensation matrix, Brady's 2,4-DNP test, and the classic semicarbazide nucleophilicity trap.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3. Ammonia Derivatives Matrix & Brady's Reagent
conceptBreakdown.title: 3. Ammonia Derivatives Matrix & Brady's Reagent

summaryBox.title: pH 3.5 & Condensation Matrix
summaryBox.takeaway: Optimal pH is ~3.5. At low pH (<2), amine is protonated and lost as nucleophile; at high pH (>6), carbonyl is not activated. Brady's 2,4-DNP gives colored ppt with all carbonyls.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
AMMONIA DERIVATIVES MATRIX
                          
   REAGENT ($H_2\text{N-Z}$)         $Z$ GROUP               CONDENSATION PRODUCT
   Hydroxylamine                     $-\text{OH}$             **Oxime** ($>\text{C=N-OH}$)
   Hydrazine                         $-\text{NH}_2$           **Hydrazone** ($>\text{C=N-NH}_2$)
   Phenylhydrazine                   $-\text{NHPh}$          **Phenylhydrazone** ($>\text{C=N-NHPh}$)
   2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine        $-\text{NH-C}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2$ **2,4-DNP Hydrazone** (Orange/Yellow Ppt)
   Semicarbazide                     $-\text{NH-CONH}_2$      **Semicarbazone** ($>\text{C=N-NH-CONH}_2$)
conceptBreakdown.content: Condensation of primary amine derivatives ($H_2\text{N-Z}$) with carbonyls requires a carefully controlled pH of ~3.5. Brady's reagent (2,4-DNP) is the universal diagnostic test for aldehydes and ketones.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.1 The Semicarbazide Nucleophilicity Trap
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 The Semicarbazide Nucleophilicity Trap
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SEMICARBAZIDE NUCLEOPHILICITY SELECTION:

• Formula: H₂N⁽¹⁾-NH-CO-NH₂⁽²⁾
• NH₂⁽¹⁾ (Hydrazine end): Isolated lone pair ──► Highly Nucleophilic (Reacts with C=O)
• NH₂⁽²⁾ (Amide end):     Lone pair delocalized into C=O via resonance: 
                          H₂N-C(=O)-NH₂ ⟷ H₂N-C(O⁻)=NH₂⁺ ──► NON-NUCLEOPHILIC!
conceptBreakdown.content: In semicarbazide, only the hydrazine $-NH_2^{(1)}$ participates in condensation. The amide $-NH_2^{(2)}$ electrons are delocalized into the carbonyl group via resonance and cannot act as a nucleophile.

quickRevision: Optimum pH for ammonia derivative condensation is ~3.5.
2,4-DNP (Brady's reagent) forms yellow/orange/red crystalline ppt with all carbonyls.
Hydroxylamine forms Oximes; Semicarbazide forms Semicarbazones.
In semicarbazide, only the hydrazine -NH₂ is nucleophilic (amide -NH₂ is resonance-delocalized).
